title: International organizations and decolonization
full_query:
Hello, I am researching the complex relationship between international organizations and decolonization in the 20th century. I hope you can help me compile a detailed report, with a deadline until early 2022. The report needs to clearly outline this history and be divided into three main parts:

Part One, regarding the period from after World War I until the end of World War II. Please focus on the dual role of the League of Nations in decolonization. On the one hand, please explain how the League maintained imperial interests through the Mandates System; on the other hand, also explain how it inadvertently provided a stage for international oversight of colonial affairs. Additionally, please introduce anti-imperialist organizations that emerged during the same period and stood in opposition to the League, especially the "League Against Imperialism", detailing its founding background, main activities, and impact.

Part Two, regarding the period of the United Nations after World War II. Please outline the role of the United Nations in the process of decolonization. This section needs to include: the United Nations' initial stance on colonial issues at its founding, the evolution from the League of Nations' Mandates System to the United Nations' Trusteeship System, and the provisions in the UN Charter concerning non-self-governing territories. Please explain in particular detail how the United Nations General Assembly and its subsidiary committees (e.g., the "Committee on Information from Non-Self-Governing Territories") became the main arena for anti-colonial struggles, and explain the historical significance and main content of the 1960 "Declaration on the Granting of Independence to Colonial Countries and Peoples."

Part Three, regarding the impact of decolonization on international organizations themselves. Please analyze how the large number of former colonial states joining the United Nations changed the agenda and power dynamics of the UN and other international organizations. Specifically, explain how international issues shifted from an "East-West confrontation" to a "North-South divide", and introduce the rise of the "Non-Alignment Movement" and the "Group of 77", as well as the background and objectives of their promotion of a "New International Economic Order" (NIEO). At the same time, also briefly mention how decolonization spurred new functions for the United Nations, such as peacekeeping operations.

Throughout the report, please use clear language, avoid simplistic dichotomies of praise or condemnation, and demonstrate the complexity of the relationship between the two. Thank you!

**important**The following is a rule of highest priority that you must not violate. Please put this rule in your task plan and keep it in your memory: **During the research process, you are not allowed to view the following article and urls: {'title': 'Special issue introduction: Towards a global history of international organizations and decolonization', 'authors': ['Eva-Maria Muschik'], 'urls': ['https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/journal-of-global-history/article/special-issue-introduction-towards-a-global-history-of-international-organizations-and-decolonization/066AFEF8CEA16E7F776CC7CFF72927CC', 'https://ideas.repec.org/a/cup/jglhis/v17y2022i2p173-190_1.html', 'https://www.researchgate.net/publication/359174525_Special_issue_introduction_Towards_a_global_history_of_international_organizations_and_decolonization', 'https://ucrisportal.univie.ac.at/en/publications/towards-a-global-history-of-international-organizations-and-decol']}. Even if you accidentally read it, please ignore the content of the article and do not quote it.**

pointwise.title: The League's dual role
pointwise.question: Does the report describe both the Mandates System's protection of imperial interests and the opening it created for international scrutiny?

anchors.1: Neither role is described.
anchors.2: Only praises or condemns the League without a concrete institutional account.
anchors.3: One role is concrete but the other is absent or merely asserted, or the mandates' welfare/development justification is omitted despite describing administration and scrutiny.
anchors.4: Both roles and their institutions are clear, with a minor territorial or procedural gap.
anchors.5: Identifies imperial administration under mandates, its stated welfare/development obligations and international reporting/review through the Permanent Mandates Commission, with territorial scope and limits clear.

pointwise.boundary: The two sides define the requested dual role; one strong side with the other missing scores 3. Explain the mandates' stated welfare/development obligations alongside imperial administration; identifying scrutiny alone does not explain that legitimating framework. Do not require named historians, British India or a fixed Article 22 quotation. Causal force is compared in PW.D3.01.

query_quotes: dual role of the League of Nations
provenance.change_note: Retain the institutional dual-role content, allowing explained qualifications; remove expert-name and exact-word requirements. Cross-review makes the already-required welfare/development framework explicit in 3/5 anchors.

anchors.5: Explains founding setting, concrete international anti-imperialist organizing and impact, including how communist/Comintern support and organizational tensions affected reach and limitations without imposing a single cause of decline.

pointwise.boundary: Brussels 1927 and Comintern-linked organization are official checking leads, not authority to ignore better-supported qualifications. Do not require Berlin, Münzenberg or a predetermined single cause of decline. The LAI alone can satisfy the emphasized organization request without a fixed count of other groups.

author_notes: Batch6 mechanical checks passed for unchanged queries, unique IDs, five-level anchors, D1–D6 coverage, per-item atomicity records and complete bidirectional official mappings. This is not independent semantic review or external verification of official facts.

No earlier draft for this assigned task was present. PT covers the named historical accounts, institutions, groupings and scope; PW compares actual mechanisms, historical synthesis, evidence and reading value without a fixed theory route.

Mixed coverage is explicitly anchored: one League role, one grouping, or only declaration content/significance scores 3. Transitions, provisions with territorial scope, and causal chains are kept together.

Official chronology and categories require care: Chapter XI versus trusteeship, information-committee institutional lineage, NIEO event dates, LAI decline versus termination and first peacekeeping missions. The original precise claims are not externally verified here; losses are recorded individually rather than described as fully covered.

Author atomicity and official-discrimination checks only, with bounded mechanical validation. No browser, reports, scores or independent reviewer was used; independent semantic review remains pending.
